title: Automated Rollout Recovery with Sticky-Session Preservation and Shadow Replay Anchors
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an automated recovery path for failed canaries that preserves session stickiness and replays shadow traffic anchors for deterministic rollback verification.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers reported two recurring issues during canary rollouts: (1) when a canary triggered a rollback, long-lived sessions lost affinity and experienced elevated error rates during the failback window; (2) shadow traffic replay tools could not deterministically reproduce the failing path because session-dependent inputs were lost at promotion time. This PR implements an automated recovery flow that (a) preserves per-session routing affinity across rollbacks, and (b) records/replays 'shadow anchors' — compact session keys and prefix traces — so post-mortem and automated regression checks can replay the exact request context.

Summary of changes: Implement a RolloutRecovery controller that tracks a sticky_session_map for affected cohorts, extends the shadow-capture pipeline to emit lightweight anchors, and adds a replay-based rollback verifier that uses anchors to validate that the rollback candidate matches production failure signals. Changes are backward compatible: when sticky sessions are not enabled for a route, the controller is a no-op.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4512)
- [x] Unit + integration tests for controller logic
- [x] E2E smoke test in perf-canary lab
- [x] Telemetry: added metrics for anchor hit/miss and session-preserve success
- [x] Rolling upgrade strategy for controller state (no single-point blocking restart)

Commits (high level):
- feat(recovery): add RolloutRecovery controller and APIs (authoritative state machine + reconciliation loop)
- feat(shadow): emit shadow_anchor tokens with session prefixes in capture pipeline
- feat(router): extend router to consult sticky_session_map on promote/rollback paths
- test: add unit tests for anchor serializer and replay verifier
- infra: add small migration to persist sticky_session_map in cluster-backed shard

Files changed (high level):
- services/rollout/controller/recovery_controller.go (core reconciliation logic; 280 LOC)
- services/router/session_affinity.go (session mapping helpers; 60 LOC)
- services/shadow/capture_pipeline.go (anchor emission; 48 LOC)
- pkg/telemetry/metrics.go (new counters: anchor_emitted, anchor_hit, session_preserve_success)
- deployments/migrations/20241010_sticky_session_map.sql (small migration)
- test/rollout/recovery_test.go (integration scenarios)
- docs/rollouts/sticky-session.md (how to enable + safety notes)

Design notes and safety guards (in-line in code):
- Sticky session map is scoped by cohort ID and has TTL eviction; entries are not a persistent user-facing privacy artifact (anchors are hashed with per-tenant salt).
- Anchors are minimized payloads (session prefix + stable-hash of request context) to avoid PII and reduce bandwidth for replay.
- Replay verifier runs on dedicated canary nodes with CPU-limited replay workers to avoid noisy-neighbor effects.
- Rollback only proceeds automatically if replay verifier confirms >95% alignment with observed failure signals OR operator-approved fast rollback is enabled.

Review conversation (summary):
- Diego Alvarez: asked for clarity on consistency model for sticky_session_map during control-plane failover. Author response: added migration to shard map and added reconciliation idempotency checks; noted that ephemeral inconsistencies are tolerated by using TTL and client-side retry.
- Priya Patel: requested privacy audit for anchor payloads. Author response: anchors are salted+hashed per-tenant; added test vectors and a small note in docs/rollouts/sticky-session.md.
- Jonas Müller: flagged potential perf regression for high-QPS routes. Author response: added adaptive sampling in capture pipeline (default 1% for high QPS) and documented policy in README. Jonas approved after perf numbers from perf-canary lab showed median p99 diff < 2ms.

CI and checks:
- unit-tests: passed (202s)
- integration-tests (rollout suite): passed (8m)
- lint: passed
- security-scan (Snyk): passed (no new high severity findings)
- perf-canary (internal): baseline run passed; measured anchor emit path with 1% sampling, CPU increase <1%.

Manual validation performed:
- Deployed feature branch to perf-canary environment with a synthetic cohort that simulates long-lived sessions and deliberate regressions.
- Triggered a canary that fails on a session-scoped bug; validated that (1) sessions remained pinned to fallback model, (2) anchors were recorded and used by the replay verifier, (3) automated rollback proceeded after replay alignment threshold was satisfied.

Backward compatibility and upgrade path:
- Controller can be deployed incrementally: when older routers that do not understand anchors receive traffic, anchors are ignored and no behavior change occurs. Migration writes a shard entry that is optional; controllers reconcile if present.

Operational runbook excerpt (docs/rollouts/sticky-session.md):
- When a canary fails but rollback verifier reports low alignment (<40%), open an incident and consider operator replay with extended anchor window.
- TTL for sticky_session_map defaults to 24h and can be tuned per-route.
- Anchor sampling rate defaults to 1% for routes with >10k RPS, 5% otherwise.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main on 2024-10-17 by Maya Chen after two approvals. CI green on final run. Post-merge actions: rolling deployment to canary fleet staged over 2 hours, perf monitoring dashboard added to Redwood Console under 'Rollouts / Sticky Session Recovery'.

Notes / follow-ups:
- Future: expose replay-based alignment score via API so customers can query rollback confidence per-deployment.
- Future: investigate integrating anchor replay into eval-harness for deterministic regression tests.
